title: Cohomology in a weak Serre class gives a triangulated subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $D(\mathcal A)$ and $H^q$ be its derived category and cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a strictly full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ containing zero, containing the kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal A$ of all morphisms between its objects, and closed under extensions: if $0\to B_1\to E\to B_2\to0$ is short exact with $B_1,B_2\in\mathcal B$, then $E\in\mathcal B$. The full subcategory $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ of objects $K$ with $H^q(K)\in\mathcal B$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$ is a strictly full triangulated subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$. Its intersections with $D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $D^b(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] are also full triangulated subcategories with the inherited shifts and distinguished triangles. Here full triangulated subcategory has the inherited structure of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].
